objective: Test whether a lower-capacity pretraining pair head improves frozen topology transfer, including its incremental value beyond the independently trained NT-conditioned branch.
reason: The selected MLP-head topology branch has variable reconstruction across seeds and weak or mixed incremental cCRE benefit after Q and handcrafted statistics. Reconstruction-selected architecture need not maximize biological reuse.
development_status: Adaptively motivated follow-up on already inspected fold A; not independent replication. TraitGym scores are not used to select this intervention.
intervention: Use the already completed bidirectional_linear topology checkpoint from the fixed four-arm reconstruction pilot instead of bidirectional_default. No additional epochs, graph changes, input changes, or biological encoder fine-tuning.

fixed.partition: development_validation only; no held-out chromosome scoring
fixed.topology_branch: Same 48-dimensional bidirectional encoder with seven visible-graph inputs and geometry-matched junction-repair objective; linear interaction pair scorer used during its existing pretraining
fixed.sequence_branch: Existing independently pretrained 48-dimensional NT-conditioned graph branch, unchanged checkpoint
fixed.random_control: Existing matched-configuration frozen random topology encoder from the same linear-head pilot; historical trained checkpoint lacks the starting-weight checksum, so exact initialization identity remains unverified
fixed.representation: Ordered frozen [T,Q] concatenation with all four trained/partial-random/random combinations
fixed.probe: Existing logistic probe with uniform max_iter=4000; same examples, calibration, regularization, solver, tolerance and feature construction

reuse: Use the completed converged seed-42 NT-only and NT-random probes, with exact baseline/example identity and numerical-budget checks; do not refit unchanged arms unnecessarily
contrasts: Linear-head T_Q minus each of its matched-dimension random/partial-random controls
Linear-head versus MLP-head T_Q after C+S and C+S+H
Linear-head T only versus MLP-head T only
Linear-head T_Q versus unchanged Q alone
validity_gates: Every input and checkpoint provenance check passes
Identical biological examples, labels and C+S/C+S+H predictions
Preserve both favorable and unfavorable task contrasts
decision: A candidate is eligible only for further development if it improves over the MLP-head composite on both tasks after C+S+H and passes all original per-seed random-control gates. Any such improvement remains exploratory; do not promote it directly to a best-model or confirmatory claim.
failure: Retain all results and do not expand an unsuccessful head change to the full matrix. Test richer allele/path representations only after verified correspondence and data support.
novelty: A weak head is a standard design choice and not a standalone novelty claim. This experiment tests transfer behavior of the audited pangenome-specific pretraining task.
